authoring: Conversation reasoning and directly authored Korean rows; no external LLM API or script-generated mechanisms.
scope_convention: reference_section means only the specifically returned text sections read, never an assertion that every page or cited reference was read. publisher_abstract includes an original author's repository abstract. stored_search_excerpt means publisher/author text returned in search; landing-page access alone is not full-text review.
comparison: All baseline key vocabulary and physical-domain principles were inspected; candidate-specific English and Korean searches also spanned the current canonical catalog across every group. The TSV contains the explicit closest existing mechanisms and a reasoned boundary. This is a semantic review, not a claim that keyword existence alone proves novelty. Parent integration review remains appropriate for parent/submechanism pairs.

evidence.read: Section 2.1, equations 2.1–2.4 and surrounding orientation/orbit text; introductory wall limitations.
evidence.quote: their orientation changes were determined by the rates of strain and rotation
evidence.support: Shape factor in orientation equation; periodic tumbling and closed kayaking orbits; wall constraints change dynamics. Primary 2025 numerical investigation uses the classical model; this is not a claim to have read Jeffery's 1922 original.

evidence.read: Section 1 equations 2–4 and Taylor expansion; concluding limitations.
evidence.quote: the first order Faxén correction accounts for the curvature of the unperturbed flow at the particle location
evidence.support: Surface-average drag and volume-average inertia replace point values. Low particle/shear Reynolds assumptions and finite-Re corrections are explicit. The paper does not solve every acceleration-PDF discrepancy.

evidence.read: Indexed publisher abstract and introduction from original 2025 study.
evidence.quote: half the mass of the fluid displaced by the sphere
evidence.support: Potential-flow accelerating sphere has acceleration-proportional force; neighbors and configuration modify tensor coefficients. Independent corroboration: Odar and Hamilton 1964 Forces on a sphere accelerating in a viscous fluid distinguishes velocity, acceleration and history forces (indexed publisher abstract).

evidence.read: Original 1967 publisher abstract returned in search.
evidence.quote: unstable at however small a Reynolds number
evidence.support: Two superposed fluids with different viscosities in Couette–Poiseuille flow can become unstable; no separate Kelvin–Helmholtz or porous-front displacement assumption. Card deliberately avoids an unverified universal stability criterion.

evidence.read: Caltech's original August 1960 technical-report abstract, lines 14–20.
evidence.quote: in second order a net inflow of gas into the bubble
evidence.support: Expansion uptake and compression loss cancel only in first order. Isothermal small-amplitude model stresses convection in the diffusion process. Area and diffusion-layer asymmetry also checked in indexed primary JFM 951 A12 (2022), A tractable mathematical model for rectified diffusion, DOI 10.1017/jfm.2022.849.

evidence.read: Indexed publisher Section 2 experiment and buoyancy-frequency definition.
evidence.quote: A salt stratification with linear density profile giving a constant buoyancy frequency
evidence.support: Experiment creates a measured stable density gradient and internal wave field, with N squared defined by negative vertical density gradient. Additional original Thorpe paper Statically unstable layers produced by overturning internal gravity waves supports large-amplitude overturning limitation. Explicit narrower dynamic propagation boundary against static density-stratification parent.

evidence.read: Publisher abstract and introduction of original 2026 experiment.
evidence.quote: For rotation rates when Coriolis forces dominate the dynamics
evidence.support: PIV extracts inertial-wave modes around vortex rings in rotating water; measured dispersion agrees with rotating-fluid prediction. The statement about Coriolis restoration is the physical interpretation of the documented wave mechanism. Distinct from spatial PV-gradient Rossby restoration and from parametric excitation of already-existing inertial waves.

evidence.read: Original Fetter author abstract, including long-wave dispersion and Biot–Savart extension.
evidence.quote: the line's curvature dominates the dynamics
evidence.support: Single vortex supports helical traveling waves; core length enters dispersion; confinement changes modes. Not a separate carrier-specific copy of lattice Tkachenko shear.

evidence.read: Abstract; introductory stable-flow transient amplification discussion; Section 4/figures 11–12 and conclusions on two-stage amplification.
evidence.quote: initial streamwise vortices transform into high and low-velocity longitudinal streaks
evidence.support: Lift-up creates streaks, then Orr tilting amplifies perturbations; nonlinear outcomes include either sustained turbulence or relaminarization. This author manuscript is labeled arXiv in the TSV because the opened record contains no journal-reference binding. A Trefethen 1993 author PDF was located but its image-only pages were not substantively read; it is not the card's evidence.

evidence.read: Booker–Bretherton original 1967 publisher abstract returned by search; DOI open failed.
evidence.quote: U is equal to the horizontal phase speed, and momentum is transferred to the mean flow there
evidence.support: Small-amplitude Boussinesq inviscid adiabatic analysis; Richardson number everywhere above one quarter; explicit attenuation factor. Does not assert all finite-amplitude critical layers completely absorb waves.

evidence.read: Author-repository original PDF indexed text around interface jump equations 7–12.
evidence.quote: derives from the strong expansion due to the phase change, which leads to the Stefan flow
evidence.support: Velocity jump distinguished from recoil pressure and Marangoni stress; mass conservation crosses phase interface. Additional primary JCP 507 112955 (2024) explicitly includes Stefan flow in multicomponent evaporation and distinguishes a pure-diffusion benchmark.

evidence.read: Original 1950 two-page letter, paragraphs around Fig. 3 and fixed end points, parsed PDF lines 63–89.
evidence.quote: A suitable applied shear stress will cause BC to curve
evidence.support: Anchored endpoints, successive closed loops, spacing-dependent minimum stress and activation below threshold. The adjacent Seitz prismatic-punching letter is not claimed as another counted mechanism.

evidence.read: Results section on mechanical instabilities and Considère maximum-load condition, plus hardening measurements.
evidence.quote: the critical point of maximum load described by the Considère criterion
evidence.support: Direct experiment/simulation paper distinguishes diffuse necking from localized necking and fracture. Cross-section reduction versus hardening is the standard mechanical interpretation of its maximum-load criterion; card does not export numerical uniform-strain predictions to rate-sensitive or thermal conditions.

evidence.read: Original PRL author's revised abstract.
evidence.quote: the system is linearly stable but nonlinearly unstable with no energy barrier
evidence.support: Purely elastic surface furrows, scale-free subcritical nonlinear instability, loading/unloading critical strains and confirming experiment. Not interpreted as a finite nucleation barrier; condition only requires nonlinear shape change.

evidence.read: Original Rice–Tracey 1969 publisher abstract returned in search; direct open returned 403.
evidence.quote: a process enhanced by the superposition of hydrostatic tensile stresses on a plastic deformation field
evidence.support: Growth/coalescence of microscopic voids in ductile fracture; source full paper was not accessible through publisher open, so detailed growth-law constants are not asserted.

evidence.read: Methods: Crack closure analyses, lines 227–235.
evidence.quote: derived from the plastically-strained crack wake
evidence.support: Original experiment explicitly separates plasticity-induced from roughness-induced closure, contact reduces effective stress-intensity range, and closure slows growth at equal nominal range. No claim that hydrogen is required for closure.

evidence.read: Original PRE author abstract and journal binding.
evidence.quote: detachment fronts that mediate inhomogeneous sliding between an elastomer and a hard surface
evidence.support: High-speed in situ displacement imaging of single waves, nucleation and pinning. Detachment/reattachment interpretation additionally corroborated by original Ringoot et al. arXiv:2011.13051 abstract. Retain only one slow-wave mechanism, not opposite directions or different elastomers as extra cards.

evidence.read: Indexed original introduction and finite-temperature glide section describing Fig. 3.
evidence.quote: nucleation of kink pairs along the straight screw dislocation, followed by lateral glide of the kinks
evidence.support: Thermally activated passage to next Peierls valley; DFT-benchmarked atomistic model; high simulation stresses reflect short observation time. Distinguishes same-plane glide from cross-slip and vacancy climb.

evidence.read: Original 2020 publisher abstract returned in search.
evidence.quote: the wall-normal gradient in turbulence intensity causes inertial particles to move preferentially toward the wall
evidence.support: Conservation-equation analysis qualifies the interpretation at small Stokes numbers; at higher Stokes number concentration relates inversely to particle velocity variance. This is not ordinary diffusion down concentration gradient or collision-induced migration.

evidence.read: Introduction paragraphs around Fig. 1, lines 54–69; abstract.
evidence.quote: subjected to an extensional strain-rate along its axis of rotation will have its cross-section reduced
evidence.support: Following paragraph states enhanced vorticity with Kelvin conservation. Original DNS study emphasizes strain self-amplification also contributes, often more to energy transfer; the card therefore never calls stretching the unique cascade cause.

exclusions.candidate: Solutal Marangoni / streaming subtypes / primary Bjerknes
exclusions.reason: Concentration, geometry or force application alone did not establish an independent microscopic route beyond existing cards.
Existing vibrated-granular-size-segregation already includes small-particle passage through gaps.
Existing contact-line-defect-barrier-hysteresis is the direct mechanism match.
Held pending explicit ideal-elastic versus fracture scope; modern work warns against treating all observed cavities as purely elastic instability.
Not included in this batch: dimensional hydrodynamic crossover needs stronger comparison to existing drag/diffusion cards and biochemical-agent coordination.
